s1.syndrome_frame: Acute flank pain with radiating groin pain in a patient with end-stage renal disease
salient_findings: Sudden onset of cramping right flank pain radiating to the groin
Tenderness at the right renal angle
Retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney
Expanding hematoma within and outside the renal capsule
key_facts: 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on thrice-weekly hemodialysis
Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel changes, or prior similar pain
Anuric for two years
Medical history includes diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and ESRD
No history of trauma or prior renal procedures
Heart rate 120 bpm, blood pressure 130/70 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Hemoglobin 6.5 g/dL and hematocrit 28%, down from baseline
Point-of-care ultrasound showed heterogeneous echogenicity around the right renal parenchyma
Emergent contrast-enhanced CT scan revealed large retroperitoneal hemorrhage
Developed worsening anemia and features of hemorrhagic shock over two days

shortlist.label: Spontaneous renal hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden onset of cramping right flank pain radiating to the groin and had a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney on CT scan

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan revealed a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney extending into the pelvis

shortlist.label: Angiomyolipoma rupture
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of spontaneous renal hemorrhage, especially in a patient with end-stage renal disease

shortlist.label: Renal artery aneurysm rupture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has vascular risk factors and presented with sudden onset of flank pain and hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Renal infarction with hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a sudden drop in hemoglobin and hematocrit, and CT scan showed an expanding hematoma within and outside the renal capsule

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden onset of cramping right flank pain, tenderness at the right renal angle, and laboratory studies showing a significant drop in hemoglobin and hematocrit, along with imaging findings of a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney, are consistent with spontaneous renal hemorrhage, particularly in the context of his underlying end-stage renal disease and lack of trauma history.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage
rejected.why: While the patient does have a retroperitoneal hemorrhage, this is more of a descriptive finding rather than a specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Angiomyolipoma rupture
rejected.why: There is no mention of a pre-existing angiomyolipoma, which is typically a prerequisite for this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Renal artery aneurysm rupture
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided to suggest the presence of a renal artery aneurysm, such as characteristic imaging findings.

rejected.label: Renal infarction with hemorrhage
rejected.why: While renal infarction could potentially lead to hemorrhage, the primary presentation and imaging findings do not strongly support infarction as the initial event.
